summary.title: Enabling Real-Time Conversations with Minimal Training Costs
summary.authors: Wang Xu, Shuo Wang, Weilin Zhao, Xu Han, Yukun Yan, Yudi Zhang, Zhe Tao, Zhiyuan Liu, Wanxiang Che
summary.executive_summary: Large language models (LLMs) typically operate on a turn-based paradigm, which precludes real-time interaction during response generation. To address this, duplex models have been proposed to facilitate real-time interactive feedback, but they often require substantial computational resources for retraining. This paper presents DUO (DUplex decOding), a novel channel-based parallel decoding mechanism that equips LLMs with duplex capabilities using minimal additional training. DUO employs a channel-division-multiplexing strategy, allowing the model to generate output autoregressively while simultaneously processing input tokens. Two state tokens are introduced to signal whether a query should be addressed or ignored, enabling the model to handle interruptions and non-awakening interactions effectively. The method is implemented using FlexAttention to manage non-standard attention mechanisms without increasing the number of forward passes compared to standard decoding. Experiments were conducted using MiniCPM-2.4B as the foundation model, trained on only 10K samples, compared to MiniCPM-Duplex which required approximately 5,000K samples. Human evaluation results indicate that DUO significantly enhances the naturalness and human-likeness of user-AI interactions while maintaining comparable levels of factuality and faithfulness. Standard benchmark evaluations show that DUO preserves the original capabilities of the base model to a greater extent than MiniCPM-Duplex, which suffers performance drops when trained on smaller datasets. The study demonstrates that DUO achieves real-time interactive feedback, including handling interruptions and filtering background dialogues, with significantly lower training costs (25 minutes on 8 GPUs vs. 36 hours on 40 GPUs). Future work aims to extend DUO to multimodal settings, where input tokens could be features extracted from various modalities.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
Large language models (LLMs) typically operate on a turn-based paradigm, which precludes real-time interaction during response generation. To address this, duplex models have been proposed to facilitate real-time interactive feedback, but they often require substantial computational resources for retraining. This paper presents DUO (DUplex decOding), a novel channel-based parallel decoding mechanism that equips LLMs with duplex capabilities using minimal additional training. DUO employs a channel-division-multiplexing strategy, allowing the model to generate output autoregressively while simultaneously processing input tokens. Two state tokens are introduced to signal whether a query should be addressed or ignored, enabling the model to handle interruptions and non-awakening interactions effectively. The method is implemented using FlexAttention to manage non-standard attention mechanisms without increasing the number of forward passes compared to standard decoding. Experiments were conducted using MiniCPM-2.4B as the foundation model, trained on only 10K samples, compared to MiniCPM-Duplex which required approximately 5,000K samples. Human evaluation results indicate that DUO significantly enhances the naturalness and human-likeness of user-AI interactions while maintaining comparable levels of factuality and faithfulness. Standard benchmark evaluations show that DUO preserves the original capabilities of the base model to a greater extent than MiniCPM-Duplex, which suffers performance drops when trained on smaller datasets. The study demonstrates that DUO achieves real-time interactive feedback, including handling interruptions and filtering background dialogues, with significantly lower training costs (25 minutes on 8 GPUs vs. 36 hours on 40 GPUs). Future work aims to extend DUO to multimodal settings, where input tokens could be features extracted from various modalities.

Research Context
Conventional LLM-powered dialogue systems operate on a turn-based paradigm. This paradigm precludes real-time interaction during response generation. Researchers have proposed duplex models to address this limitation. These models can dynamically adapt to user input. However, these methods typically require substantial computational resources. Existing approaches like MiniCPM-Duplex use time-division-multiplexing strategies. This approach requires significant resources due to divergent training procedures. The gap is the high overhead of acquiring duplex ability.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The hypothesis is that a channel-division-multiplexing decoding strategy can enable duplex ability. The method predicts that parallel decoding of queries and responses will work. It is hypothesized that minimal additional training is sufficient for this capability. The study aims to enhance the naturalness and human-likeness of interactions. The predicted outcome is that the model can handle interruptions effectively. The approach is expected to preserve the original model's capabilities. The hypothesis includes the ability to filter non-query inputs.

Methodological Details
The study uses MiniCPM-2.4B as the foundation model. A dataset of 10K samples was constructed for training. The dataset was adapted from Duplex-UltraChat. Two state tokens were introduced to indicate query status. State token <1> denotes that the input is a user query. State token <2> denotes that the new input is no-query text. Non-query text was generated using ChatGPT. The training used a learning rate of 1e-5. A constant learning rate scheduler was employed. The batch size was set to 112. The maximum sequence length was 4,096. Training was conducted for 400 steps. The model was trained on 8 NVIDIA A100 GPUs. The total training time was approximately 25 minutes. The baseline MiniCPM-Duplex was trained for 10,000 steps. The baseline used 40 NVIDIA A100 GPUs. The baseline training time was 36 hours. The input channel predicted tokens alpha were set to 4.

Procedures And Architectures
DUO processes inputs and outputs cyclically. The output channel generates new tokens autoregressively. The input channel pre-fills the key-value cache. A channel-aware causal mask is used for attention. Tokens from input and output channels do not attend to each other. This preserves language modeling in each channel. Channel transition is activated when state tokens are predicted. DUO does not increase the number of forward passes. The decoding strategy is based on the Ouroboros repository. The model decides whether a query is addressed or ignored. The input channel predicts the next tokens. The output channel persists in generating tokens. The key-value cache of predicted tokens is managed.

Key Results
MiniCPM-Duo demonstrates superior responsiveness compared to MiniCPM-Duplex. MiniCPM-Duo shows better human-likeness than the baseline. Factuality levels are comparable between the two models. Faithfulness is maintained at similar levels. MiniCPM-Duo exhibits a substantial advantage in overall performance. On CMMLU, MiniCPM-Duo achieved a score of 50.66. On MMLU, MiniCPM-Duo achieved a score of 53.13. On BBH, MiniCPM-Duo achieved a score of 36.51. On HumanEval, MiniCPM-Duo achieved a score of 51.83. On MBPP, MiniCPM-Duo achieved a score of 38.19. On GSM8K, MiniCPM-Duo achieved a score of 42.15. On ARC-e, MiniCPM-Duo achieved a score of 84.93. On ARC-c, MiniCPM-Duo achieved a score of 70.48. On HellaSwag, MiniCPM-Duo achieved a score of 59.78. MiniCPM-Duplex trained on 10K samples showed performance drops. The duplex capability of inadequately trained MiniCPM-Duplex was poor.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The method effectively implements channel-division-multiplexing decoding. This approach preserves the original model's capabilities. The minimal training cost is a significant theoretical advantage. The model can handle non-awakening interactions effectively. The state tokens provide a mechanism for query filtering. The approach is versatile and adaptable to multimodal settings. The method enhances the fluidity of human-AI interaction. The results support the hypothesis of efficient duplex learning.

Contradictions And Limitations
The study has limitations in the scope of multimodal testing. Experiments primarily focused on language models. This may limit the generalizability of findings. The dataset size is significantly smaller than the baseline. The human evaluation involved only three participants. The evaluation was based on 40 dialogue sessions.

Claims
DUO enables real-time conversations with minimal training costs. The method requires minimal additional training. Training took only 25 minutes. Only 10K samples were used. The baseline required 36 hours of training. The baseline used 5,000K samples. 
DUO enhances the naturalness and human-likeness of interactions. MiniCPM-Duo shows superior human-likeness. It demonstrates superior responsiveness. Factuality and faithfulness are comparable, not superior. It makes interactions more fluid.

Data And Code Availability
The decoding strategy is based on the Ouroboros repository. An interactive demo is available for MiniCPM-Duplex. The dataset was constructed from Duplex-UltraChat.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
The study compares DUO with MiniCPM-Duplex trained on the same data scale. MiniCPM-Duplex showed performance drops with smaller data. DUO preserves original capabilities better.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1 illustrates the channel-based parallel decoding. Figure 2 shows the human evaluation comparison. Figure 3 presents a case study of the model's behavior. Table 1 presents performances on standard benchmarks.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is the DUO decoding method. 2. The strongest evidence is the minimal training cost. 3. The future path is extending to multimodal settings.
